newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine decree on health-plan reform imminent.
newsitem.headline: Argentine decree on health-plan reform imminent.

text.p: President Carlos Menem will sign a decree later Monday or Tuesday deregulating the union controlled health-care system to allow Argentines to choose their own medical plans, an official in the presidency said.
Argentina now has more than 300 union-controlled health plans financed by mandatory contributions, which bring in about $2.5 billion a year to the unions.
Under the reform, members would be allowed to choose from any union plan from Jan 1 and, from 1998, be able to opt out of public plans in favor of private ones.
Many of the health plans are deep in debt, and members have had to seek duplicate coverage in private schemes.
Government officials say they hope deregulation will reduce the number of union-sponsored health plans to 250 by the end of the year and to between 70 and 80 by the end of 1997.

The head of the CGT union confederation, Rodolfo Daer, told a radio interviewer Monday he was not opposed to members choosing their health plans. However, it was unclear whether he favored their right to chose a non-union system.
